answer: Jury seats are expensive by design: a seat requires a bond sized to the whole epoch's reward budget, and a panel only counts when it draws from four unrelated subnetworks. One upheld challenge voids every grade that juror has ever cast. A farm renting a timber yard of nodes cannot bridge that gap: it still cannot seat two clones on one panel without paying the bond twice, and the ocean of proxy addresses it rents does not change the subnetwork count. Fixed cost per clone, no volume discount.
